request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows a "Watched due total" for the signed-in user: the due-totals of everyone they watch, added up, or `0.00` when they watch no one. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

The app already stored who watches whom, so this was a front-end change only, in two files:

- **`src/main/frontend/features/header/totals.ts`** has a new `useWatchedDue(sheetId, user)` function. It takes the people the user watches and adds up their due-totals, using the same per-person figures their rows show. People whose due-total shows `n/a` are skipped, and it is not trimmed, unlike the sheet's own due-total, which drops the highest and lowest.
- **`src/main/frontend/features/header/header.slot.tsx`** shows the figure at the end of the header, in an element with the test id `watched-due-total`.

Nothing changed on the server or in the audit file: the watch and unwatch records the test checks were already being written.
